item.title: Foreign Funds Return to India’s Banks After $12 Billion Selloff
item.description: Global investors returned to India’s financial stocks after a three-month selling streak, as the central bank’s recent measures to draw foreign capital ease funding constraints for lenders.

item.title: India Objection to WhatsApp Username Switch Gets Somalia Backing
item.description: Somalia joined India in objecting to Meta Platforms Inc.’s planned WhatsApp username feature, citing security concerns in a country that’s been battling Islamist militants for two decades.

item.title: TalkTalk Wholesale Arm Is Said to Draw Interest From Telecel
item.description: Telecel Group is among bidders competing to acquire TalkTalk Telecom Group’s wholesale telecommunications business, people familiar with the matter said.

item.title: Panetta Sees Fragile Outlook With Risks to Inflation, Growth
item.description: The European Central Bank is navigating an uncertain economic situation even as the US and Iran move closer to a lasting peace deal, according to Governing Council member Fabio Panetta.

item.title: BAE-Backed Venture Capital Firm Expeditions Raises €197 Million Fund for European Defense Startups
item.description: A defense-tech venture capital firm backed by BAE Systems and the NATO Innovation Fund has raised a €197 million ($225 million) fund to help develop sovereign military technologies in Europe.

item.title: Czech June Inflation Slows More Than Expected After Rate Hike
item.description: Czech inflation slowed more than expected below target last month, underscoring the central bank’s monetary-policy dilemma after it raised interest rates.

item.title: Italy’s Oldest Dairy Taps New Way to Borrow Against Aging Cheese
item.description: Italy’s oldest dairy company has borrowed money against cheese still aging in its warehouse, taking advantage of a change in the law aimed at helping food and wine producers access finance.

item.title: Germany Files Charges in ‘Operation Chargeback’ Payment Scam
item.description: German prosecutors filed their first charges linked to a €300 million ($343 million) global payment-fraud that allegedly duped millions of credit card holders in a scam that enlisted the help of payment company executives.

item.title: SpaceX Wins Bullish Calls With Morgan Stanley’s Target at $300
item.description: SpaceX is winning early backing from Wall Street as global brokerages start coverage of Elon Musk’s rocket and artificial intelligence company with a clear consensus: buy the stock.

item.title: German Industry Grows More Than Expected on Auto Sector
item.description: German industrial production grew for a second month, another sign that Europe’s largest economy is exiting the drag from the Iran war.

item.title: Temasek-Backed Gym Chain Cult.Fit Files Paperwork for India IPO
item.description: Cult.Fit Ltd. has filed draft paperwork to raise about $100 million in an initial public offering, a rare debut for a gym operator in the world’s most populous country.

item.title: FTSE 100 Outperforms as Shell Drives Gains
Google and RWE Back German Nuclear Startup Proxima Fusion at €2.4 Billion Valuation
item.description: German startup Proxima Fusion has raised €411 million ($469 million) from a range of investors, including national energy firm RWE AG and Alphabet Inc.’s Google, to develop a nuclear fusion plant it hopes will be operational in the 2030s.

item.title: South Africa Treasury Cuts Johannesburg Funds Over Wage Bill
item.description: South Africa’s National Treasury will withhold state funding for Johannesburg and dozens of other municipalities this month over their failure to manage their finances properly.

item.title: AI Won’t Bring Back Era of Rapid Growth, Says Nobel Prize Winner
item.description: A Nobel Prize-winning economist has warned that artificial intelligence will not return Western economies to the era of rapid productivity growth, which may be gone forever.

item.title: Won’s 24-Hour Trading Debut Passes With Below-Average Volume
item.description: Trading in the Korean won passed with below-average volume in its first day of round-the-clock dealing during a largely uneventful session, compared to the past 30 days.

item.title: Early Forint Bull Barclays Sees Rally Fading as Euro Work Begins
item.description: The forint rally triggered by Hungary’s political shift is fading as Prime Minister Peter Magyar faces a daunting task to prepare the country for euro accession, according to a strategist at Barclays Plc.

item.title: Buy SK Hynix’s New ADRs and Sell Seoul-Listed Shares, UBS Says
item.description: Investors should purchase SK Hynix Inc.’s planned American depositary receipts and sell the chipmaker’s South Korean-traded stock as the new securities are likely to trade at a premium, according to UBS Group AG.

item.title: China Buys More US Soybeans as Key Agricultural Trade Ramps Up
item.description: China has purchased more soybeans from the US, according to people familiar with the matter, as the key agricultural trade gains momentum following a summit between the leaders of the two nations in May.

item.title: India Property Developer K Raheja Said to Delay $700 Million IPO
item.description: K Raheja Corp. Pvt., one of India’s largest real estate developers, has delayed plans for an initial public offering after feedback from investment bankers, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Europe’s Defense Stocks Rally Has Much Riding on NATO Summit
item.description: A fledgling rebound in European defense stocks faces a test this week, as investors look to a NATO summit for further clarity on member states’ defense spending plans.

item.title: Mystery Thai Investor’s Near $1 Billion True Stake Sparks Probe
item.description: Thailand’s market regulator is probing the sudden emergence of an individual shareholder who has amassed nearly $1 billion worth of shares in True Corp., making her one of the telecom giant’s largest shareholders.

item.title: A Token Grasp of the AI Boom Shows Trouble Brewing
item.description: The period of vertical ascent is probably over.

item.title: Japan’s Inpex Signs 15-Year Deal to Buy Persian Gulf LNG
item.description: Japan’s state-backed Inpex Corp. signed a 15-year deal with Abu Dhabi National Oil Co. for the supply of liquefied natural gas from its project in the Persian Gulf.

item.title: Japan 30-Year Bonds Rise After Strong Demand Reassures Investors
item.description: Japan’s 30-year government bonds rose after an auction of the tenor drew its strongest demand since 2019, as high yield levels attracted investors despite worries about fiscal policy and inflation.

item.title: PBOC Unveils New Measures to Cement Hong Kong’s Yuan Hub Status
item.description: China’s central bank announced a slew of measures aimed at expanding an investment channel between Hong Kong’s financial market and the mainland, as well as enhancing the city’s role in promoting overseas use of the yuan.

item.title: India’s Unloved Heavyweight Stocks May Be Poised for a Rebound
item.description: A combination of under-ownership and attractive valuations could draw buyers.

item.title: Samsung Results Trigger Stock Rotation to Less Loved Sectors
item.description: Asian tech stocks slumped, as investors used Samsung Electronics Co.’s results to lock in profits on a stellar year-to-date chip rally, rotating into unloved sectors less prone to earnings shocks.

item.title: Chinese Firms Leave Nvidia for Local AI Suppliers, Survey Shows
item.description: Chinese companies are ditching Nvidia Corp.’s advanced accelerators in favor of domestic silicon, underscoring how tensions with the US are reshaping the AI infrastructure buildout and propelling Beijing’s ambitions to substitute American technology.

item.title: Japan Isn’t Pushing for Low Interest Rates, Growth Minister Says
item.description: Media reports that claim Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi’s administration is attempting to keep interest rates low and weaken fiscal improvement efforts aren’t accurate at all, according to Japan’s Growth Strategy Minister Minoru Kiuchi.
